headline: Judge: FCC pressure on ABC licenses violated free speech
pages: A federal judge has blocked the Trump administration from acting to challenge ABC's broadcast licenses, calling it unconstitutional punishment for coverage the president dislikes. Judge Loren AliKhan of the US District Court in Washington issued a preliminary injunction Wednesday. She found early license reviews by the FCC were retaliation for speech, including Jimmy Kimmel's jokes, remarks on The View, and a 2024 debate. She wrote that the threat of losing licenses could chill a broadcaster of ordinary firmness. She counted eleven calls by Trump over two years to strip ABC's licenses and said FCC Chairman Brendan Carr took the rhetoric as marching orders.
She also rejected the government's motion to dismiss. ABC called the ruling an important victory for the First Amendment. Carr did not respond to NPR. Source: NPR.
